The Cloud-runner track is complete-to-the-gate through W16 (both D139 halves wired; no offline-provable cloud-runner increment remains — cloud-runner work and live/design-gated cloud items are OUT). The epic (task-e640bb01fca6ea38) has 41 open children with a real genuinely-buildable-offline backlog: filed BUGS (orphan session on mint race; thread-state keys lack workspace; catalog multi-install oldest-wins), protective-TEST gaps (bridge tool lifecycle; RequireChatAccess plug unit test), DISCOVERABILITY (chat-token mint as a capabilities core_cmd), DOCS (auth.md Roles missing chat + public-read), and DEP DEBT (connectors npm audit ~20 vulns). Sweep a coherent cluster of the highest-value buildable increments; decline every gated item with one-line evidence; every fix pins a protective test that REDS before the change. Never fake, never pad, no vacuous green.

The finished wave: 4-6 file-disjoint slices merged, each closing a REAL defect or a REAL coverage gap with a fail-first protective test, and every gated candidate declined on named evidence — the epic's open-child count drops meaningfully and honestly. This is a breadth wave (unlike W16's single slice), mixing Node-bridge and Elixir work that rides different CI gates by construction.

Tentative priority order (Decide finalizes): (1) HEADLINE — connectors-sdk-thread-state-key-lacks-workspace: a cross-tenant collision risk is a tenancy-correctness bug, the most valuable single fix on the board; the survey must nail the key shape + back-compat migration for existing rows. (3) connectors-require-chat-access-plug-unit-test: direct fail-closed coverage of the chat-perm + nil-workspace deny branches — cheap, high-protective-value, pure-additive Elixir. (4) connectors-bridge-tool-lifecycle-tests: fold the W10 verify findings into permanent CI tests. (5) connectors-chat-permission-docs-registry: mechanical Sonnet docs slice inside the byte budget. (6) connectors-chat-token-mint-capabilities-entry: WANTED but carries a contradiction — the task text says '+ openapi regen' while the wave constraint says never touch openapi; survey resolves whether the CI-artifact regen flow or a no-openapi shape exists, else the slice narrows or drops. (7) connectors-catalog-multi-install: build only if the survey proves oldest-wins is a real defect with a defined correct behavior. (8) connectors-npm-audit-debt: assess-first — ship a non-breaking upgrade proven by the vitest suite, else file the honest per-vuln residue; a breaking bump is out of scope.

Hard lines: no cloud-runner code, no human gates, no design-gated items — each declined with one-line evidence (D148 discipline). Every fix lands with a protective test pinned RED before the change. Node slices ride connectors.yml (0-skip, real Postgres); Elixir slices ride elixir.yml with the inherited-flake set re-derived fresh at merge; docs ride doc-gates. No data migration needed: affected tables hold ephemeral SDK coordination state; old rows go dead-but-harmless, state reconstructs on next inbound message. What shipped (per slice — task, final branch, verdict)

Cross-slice coherence

D165 ordering law VERIFIED by the reviewer. W17-1 and W17-2 both touch connectors/src/index.ts; a real 3-way merge (W17-1 then W17-2) auto-merges clean — the merged index.ts carries both imports (L66/L68) and both wirings (L300 scopeStateAdapter, L502 createPgLockedThreadSessionMap), tsc clean, both protective tests 18/18 green together. The lead merges W17-1 first, then W17-2. All other slices are file-disjoint (Elixir catalog, Node test files, docs, lock).

What stalled

W17-5 connectors-require-chat-access-plug-unit-test — NOT DELIVERED. The builder claimed (epoch 3, 14:15) with now-line 'building: writing struct-literal unit test' but produced NO branch, NO commit, NO evidence: the agent died mid-build. The reviewer reset the task to open backlog with a durable wave17_status note; its stale claim was reaped (worker null). It remains genuinely buildable offline — Verify already proved the require_chat_access.ex:58 nil-guard mutation-kill. This is the first pick of Wave 18.

Grade + commentary

A-. Six real increments merge-ready with proven-RED discipline and zero reviewer fixes: three genuine defects closed (a leaked Session per first-message race; a cross-tenant state collision; an undisconnectable second-install credential — a security hole), two protective-test slices covering real lifecycle/permission gaps, an accurate fact-checked docs registry addition, and a network-facing dependency-debt reduction. The wish asked for ~3-6 disjoint slices; 6 shipped, at the top of that range, holistically satisfying the ask. Docked from A by one process blemish (W17-5 silently died with no in-band signal until review) and one minor UX disambiguation gap in the catalog card. Not manufactured criticism — everything that merges is clean; the gap is what did NOT merge.

Ledger audit outcome

All six built tasks honest: each claimed (worker present), every non-merge-gate criterion stamped met=true with evidence that matches the reviewer's own re-runs, the final MERGE-GATE criterion correctly met=false with empty evidence, lifecycle in_progress — the lead closes those on merge. The declined D166 backlog (5 human gates + 5 design-gated cloud items + the capabilities-entry D162 decline) was not touched. Epic wave_status heartbeat stamped 'wave 17: COMPLETE — grade A-'.

What Wave 18 should take

First: W17-5 (require-chat-access plug unit test) — fully specced, mutation-kill already proven, just needs a builder that survives. Then continue the epic-perfection sweep across the remaining ~40 open offline-buildable children (more protective-test and discoverability gaps), holding the same no-vacuous-green bar. The cloud-runner track and all human/design-gated items stay OUT until a real key/creds/deploy or a fresh design decision lands.
